answer: An identity must be at least 4 epochs old on the falcon ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. Because the age is read from the marble checkpoint rather than self-declared, the knoll audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. Running a farm therefore means funding each extra identity through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent forfeits once and never again. That is 28 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
